# Polaris for Go

> Authentication and authorization for Go services, for users and for AI agents, self-hosted in
> your database: user sign-in (password, MFA, sessions, organizations, RBAC, passwordless, passkeys,
> social, SSO, SCIM), API keys, an OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect provider, agents as first-class
> principals (grants, budgets, approvals, signed receipts, kill switch) and MCP protection. One
> import, a few lines, net/http.

Module: `github.com/univeros/polaris.go` (Go 1.26): `go get github.com/univeros/polaris.go`.
The package name is `polaris`.

## Quickstart (copy this)

```go
import (
	polaris "github.com/univeros/polaris.go"
	"github.com/univeros/polaris.go/store"
	"github.com/univeros/polaris.go/store/sqlstore"
)

db, err := sqlstore.Open(ctx, store.Postgres, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")) // or store.MySQL, store.SQLite
cfg, err := polaris.FromEnv(db /*, plugins... */)                        // reads the env vars below
p, err := polaris.New(cfg)                                               // validates everything; errors say how to fix
_, err = p.Migrate(ctx)                                                  // creates missing tables, seeds permissions; idempotent

mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("/", p.Handler()) // every Polaris route: /auth/register, /auth/login, /auth/token/refresh, /orgs, ...
mux.Handle("GET /api/invoices", p.Protect(invoicesHandler, "org.read")) // your route, Polaris principals
// in the handler: who, ok := polaris.PrincipalFrom(r.Context()) — who.UserID, who.OrganizationID,
// who.Permissions, who.Kind (polaris.KindUser | KindAPIKey | KindOAuthClient | KindAgent), who.Delegated.
```

Environment: `APP_KEY` (≥ 32 bytes: `openssl rand -base64 32`), `AUTH_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` and
`AUTH_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY` (PEM; `openssl genrsa -out jwt.key 2048 && openssl rsa -in jwt.key -pubout -out jwt.pub`),
`AUTH_ISSUER` (your public base URL). Optional: `AUTH_AUDIENCE`, `AUTH_JWT_PREVIOUS_PUBLIC_KEY` (key
rotation), `AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_DENYLIST`, … — every option is in package `config` (`go doc config.Auth`).
EdDSA instead of RS256: `polaris keys:generate --alg=EdDSA` (base64 keys for the same two variables), then
`cfg.Auth.AccessToken.Signer = config.SignerEdDSA` before `polaris.New`; the JWKS publishes it as an OKP key.

Your own permissions: `cfg.Permissions = map[string]string{"invoices.read": "Read invoices"}` before
`polaris.New`; `Migrate` adds them to the catalog. Grant them to roles through `/orgs/{id}/roles`.

Housekeeping: schedule `p.Prune(ctx)` (hourly is plenty) to delete expired refresh tokens, codes and
invitations; idempotent on every replica.

Production ports (fields of `polaris.Config`; each has a working default, the logging ones warn):
`Mailer notify.Mailer` and `SMS notify.SMSSender` (verification / reset / OTP delivery — the
defaults only log), `Cache cache.Cache` and `RateStore` (share across replicas; a host cache must make
`Add` atomic, e.g. Redis SET NX), `Events event.Dispatcher`, `Logger *slog.Logger`, `PathPrefix`.
Host extensions: `Listeners []event.Listener` (your listeners on every domain event), `Middleware`
(wrapped outermost around `Handler` and every `Protect`: tracing, request ids), `Hooks` (below).

## Your app's own data: hooks, transactions, Go calls

```go
cfg.Hooks = polaris.Hooks{
	OnUserCreated: func(ctx context.Context, u polaris.User) error { return createProfile(ctx, u.ID) }, // same transaction as the account
	OnUserDeleted: func(ctx context.Context, userID string) error { return deleteProfile(ctx, userID) },
	Claims: func(ctx context.Context, in polaris.ClaimsInput) (map[string]any, error) {
		return map[string]any{"app_plan": planOf(in.UserID)}, nil // reserved names (sub, org, roles, …) are refused
	},
}
p, err := polaris.New(cfg)

tx, err := db.DB().BeginTx(ctx, nil)                              // your transaction (sqlstore.Store.DB() is the *sql.DB)
ada, err := p.Users().Create(sqlstore.WithTx(ctx, tx), polaris.NewUser{Email: "ada@example.com", EmailVerified: true})
err = tx.Commit()                                                 // or Rollback: the account and OnUserCreated's rows go too
org, err := p.Orgs().Create(ctx, ada.ID, "Acme", "")              // ada is its owner
err = p.Orgs().AddMember(ctx, org.ID, otherUserID, "member")
tokens, err := p.Sessions().Issue(ctx, polaris.SignIn{UserID: ada.ID}) // your own sign-in; tokens.AccessToken works on Protect
ok := p.Can(ctx, polaris.Principal{UserID: ada.ID, OrganizationID: org.ID}, "org.read")
// errors: errors.Is(err, polaris.ErrNotFound), polaris.ErrConflict, polaris.ErrForbidden, polaris.ErrInvalidInput, polaris.ErrInvalidCredentials
```

`p.Users()`: Get, ByEmail, Create, Import, SetPassword, Disable, Enable, Delete. `p.Orgs()`: Create, Get,
ListFor, AddMember, SetRoles, RemoveMember. `p.Sessions()`: Issue, Refresh, Revoke, RevokeAll. Same
rules, events and audit as the HTTP routes; the caller is trusted (no permission check).

## Migrating your users

Bring existing accounts with the password hash they have; nobody resets a password. The first
successful sign-in of each user replaces the imported hash with Argon2id.

```go
tx, err := db.DB().BeginTx(ctx, nil)
for _, row := range legacyRows { // your users table, or an Auth0 / Firebase / Django export
	_, err = p.Users().Import(sqlstore.WithTx(ctx, tx), polaris.ImportedUser{
		Email: row.Email, PasswordHash: row.PasswordHash, DisplayName: row.Name,
		EmailVerified: row.Verified, Disabled: row.Banned, CreatedAt: row.CreatedAt,
	}) // ErrInvalidInput (and security.ErrUnsupportedHash): a hash Polaris cannot verify; ErrConflict: email taken
}
err = tx.Commit() // all or nothing; OnUserCreated ran for each account, no email was sent
```

Hashes verified as they are (`security.SupportedHashFormats`): bcrypt `$2a$`/`$2b$`/`$2y$` (Auth0,
Devise, Laravel, most Go and Node apps), Argon2id/Argon2i, Django `pbkdf2_sha256$…` and `scrypt$…`,
passlib `$pbkdf2-sha256$`, `$pbkdf2-sha512$`, `$scrypt$ln=…`. Firebase: build
`fmt.Sprintf("$firebase-scrypt$ln=%d,r=%d,sep=%s,key=%s$%s$%s", memCost, rounds, saltSeparator, signerKey, salt, passwordHash)`
from the project's hash parameters and each exported user (base64 values as exported). A cost
outside sane bounds is refused. Cognito exports no hashes: import without `PasswordHash` and let
users reset, or verify them your way and call `p.Sessions().Issue`. Another scheme of your own: wrap
`security.Argon2id` as `Config.Hasher`, handling your prefix in `Verify` and `CheckHash` (`go doc
security.HashChecker`); it upgrades on sign-in the same way.

## Plugins (pass to polaris.FromEnv / Config.Plugins)

- `plugins/audit` — `audit.New(audit.Config{})`: append-only audit log of every event, sinks, drains, hash chain. Required by admin.
- `plugins/admin` — `admin.New(admin.Config{})`: operator API (`/admin/*`) for users, sessions, MFA, orgs, audit; operator keys `pak_`.
- `plugins/apikeys` — `apikeys.New(apikeys.Config{})`: user/org API keys (`pk_live_…`, `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`), scoped to a subset of the owner's permissions, rate-limited, rotatable.
- `plugins/oauth` — `oauth.New(oauth.Config{})`: OAuth 2.1 / OIDC provider (PKCE, refresh rotation, client credentials, device, CIBA, token exchange with `act`, DPoP, DCR, CIMD, discovery). Scopes are permissions.
- `plugins/agents` — `agents.New(agents.Config{Capabilities: …})`: agents as principals. Needs `oauth`.
- `plugins/mcp` — `mcp.New(mcp.Config{BaseURL: …})`: Polaris as an MCP server (`POST /mcp`, stdio); and `mcp.Protect` for your own MCP servers.
- `plugins/passwordless` — `passwordless.New(passwordless.Config{RedirectURIs: …})`: magic links, email / phone codes, one-time hand-off tokens; all behind core's MFA gate.
- `plugins/username` — `username.New(username.Config{})`: case-insensitive usernames; sign in with username or email.
- `plugins/anonymous` — `anonymous.New(anonymous.Config{OnConvert: …})`: guest sessions converted on sign-up.
- `plugins/multisession` — `multisession.New(multisession.Config{})`: several accounts per device, switch without signing in again.
- `plugins/social` — `social.New(social.Config{Providers: map[string]social.Provider{"google": {ClientID: …, ClientSecret: …}}})`: 19 OAuth/OIDC providers + generic, linking, One Tap.
- `plugins/passkey` — `passkey.New(passkey.Config{RPID: "example.com", Origins: []string{"https://example.com"}})`: WebAuthn sign-in; a passkey is also an MFA factor.
- `plugins/messaging` — `messaging.New(messaging.Config{Email: &messaging.SMTP{…}, SMS: &messaging.Twilio{…}})`: becomes core's mailer and SMS sender; templates per instance/org, translations, send caps.
- `plugins/sentinel` — `sentinel.New(sentinel.Config{})`: risk engine on sign-up, sign-in, reset and code sends (captcha, breached passwords, disposable domains, velocity, geo via your `GeoResolver`); observes by default, `Mode: sentinel.Enforce` blocks and challenges.
- `plugins/sso` — `sso.New(sso.Config{})`: SAML 2.0 and OIDC sign-in per organization, verified domains, single logout; an IdP signs in only members or users on the org's verified domains.
- `plugins/scim` — `scim.New(scim.Config{})`: SCIM 2.0 provisioning per organization with an org-managed connection token; changes global accounts only when the connection created them.

## Agents: declare what agents may do

```go
ag := agents.New(agents.Config{Capabilities: []agents.Capability{
	{Name: "invoices.list", Description: "List invoices", Permission: "org.read", Risk: agents.RiskLow,
		Handler: func(ctx context.Context, call agents.Call) (any, error) { return listInvoices(ctx, call.Agent) }},
	{Name: "refund", Description: "Refund an invoice", Permission: "billing.refund", Risk: agents.RiskHigh,
		Location: "https://app.example.com/api/refunds",
		Input: map[string]any{"type": "object", "required": []string{"invoice_id"},
			"properties": map[string]any{"invoice_id": map[string]any{"type": "string"}}}},
}})
cfg, _ := polaris.FromEnv(db, audit.New(audit.Config{}), admin.New(admin.Config{}), oauth.New(oauth.Config{}), ag)
cfg.Permissions = map[string]string{"billing.refund": "Refund an invoice"} // your own permissions; Migrate seeds them
p, _ := polaris.New(cfg)
mux.Handle("/", p.Handler()) // includes /.well-known/agent-configuration, /agents/*, /oauth2/*
mux.Handle("POST /api/refunds", ag.Protect("refund", refundHandler)) // grant, constraints, budget checked BEFORE refundHandler
// in refundHandler: call, _ := agents.CallFrom(r.Context()); the response gets X-Polaris-Receipt.
```

Risk tiers set the approval strength (low/medium: session, high: step-up). Low-risk grants are
auto-approved with a budget of 100 by default (`Config.AutoApprove`). Every execution writes a signed,
hash-chained receipt; `POST /agents/{id}/revoke` is the kill switch.

## Agents: sign in from Go (the agent side)

```go
import "github.com/univeros/polaris.go/agent"

key, _ := agent.GenerateKey(agent.EdDSA)                 // persist key.Export(); reload with agent.ImportKey
a, _ := agent.New(ctx, "https://app.example.com", agent.WithKey(key))
bot, _, err := a.Enroll(ctx, enrollmentToken, agent.Registration{Name: "Worker", Mode: agent.Delegated})
asked, _ := bot.RequestGrants(ctx, agent.GrantRequest{Capabilities: []agent.CapabilityRequest{{Name: "refund"}}})
if asked.Approval != nil { _, err = bot.WaitForApproval(ctx, *asked.Approval) } // a person approves
res, err := bot.Execute(ctx, "invoices.list", nil)       // signed request JWT per call; res.Receipt
// errors: errors.Is(err, agent.ErrCapabilityNotGranted), agent.ErrBudgetExhausted, agent.ErrApprovalDenied …
```

## Protect any Go MCP server with Polaris tokens

```go
h, err := mcp.Protect(mcpServerHandler, mcp.ProtectConfig{
	Resource: "https://tools.example.com/mcp",
	Issuer:   "https://auth.example.com",
	JWKSURL:  "https://auth.example.com/auth/.well-known/jwks.json",
	Scopes:   []string{"tools.use"},
})
mux.Handle("/", h) // also serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp; mcp.Claims(ctx) in the handler
```

## Testing your app

```go
srv := polaristest.New(t, polaristest.WithPlugins(audit.New(audit.Config{}))) // SQLite in a temp dir, test keys, recorders
// srv.Handler(), srv.Users(), srv.Sessions(), srv.Mailer.Sent() (verification tokens), srv.SMS, srv.Events.Names()
// polaristest.WithConfig(func(c *polaris.Config) { c.Hooks = … }) for anything else
```

## CLI

`go run ./cmd/polaris <command>` — every command idempotent, `--json` for one JSON object,
exit 1 (failed) / 2 (bad usage) with a `remedy:` line.

```
polaris init [--plugins=audit,admin,apikeys,oauth,agents,mcp,…]  # writes .env: APP_KEY, RS256 pair, AUTH_ISSUER; prints the quickstart
polaris migrate --plugins=…            # DATABASE_URL or --dsn (postgres://, mysql://, sqlite:, file:)
polaris doctor --plugins=…             # secrets, keys, manifest, connectivity, schema; each check with its fix
polaris schema:export --target=sql:postgres|sql:mysql|sql:sqlite   schema:diff   schema:drop --force
polaris manifest --format=json|openapi   keys:generate   mcp (stdio MCP server)
polaris audit:prune|audit:verify   admin:grant <email> <role>   admin:key <name> <role>   anonymous:prune
```

With your own plugins, build your own binary: `os.Exit(cli.Run(ctx, p, os.Args[1:], os.Stdout, os.Stderr))`.

## Errors

Core routes answer `{"error": "<code>", "message": "…"}`; plugin routes answer RFC 9457 problems
(`application/problem+json`, `type` = `https://polaris.univeros.io/problems/<plugin>/<name>`).
Go calls on `*polaris.Polaris` return `polaris.ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict`, `ErrForbidden`,
`ErrInvalidInput`, `ErrInvalidCredentials` (`errors.Is`); other packages have their own sentinels.

## Where to look

- `examples/` — complete programs (each runs with zero setup: `go run ./examples/<name>`, SQLite and
  keys generated at start; the README has the curl walkthrough with real output; `main_test.go` keeps it working):
  `minimal` (core, one protected route), `api-keys`, `agents` (capabilities in process and behind
  `ag.Protect`, an agent built with package `agent`: enrol, grants, approval, budget and constraint
  refusals, receipts, kill switch), `mcp` (your MCP server behind `mcp.Protect`, Polaris's `/mcp`,
  token exchange per resource), `b2b` (organizations, your permissions, roles, invitations, org API
  keys, audit, admin, SSO and SCIM setup), `signin-methods` (magic link, email code, username,
  guest conversion, multisession, passkey, social OIDC, messaging, sentinel, MFA), `hooks` (your own
  table kept in step by `Hooks`, `Claims`, listeners, middleware, `sqlstore.WithTx`, `Prune`).
- `plugins/<id>/README.md` — per plugin: config, routes, events, permissions, problems, hooks.
- `plugins/agents/example_test.go`, `agent/example_test.go`, `plugins/mcp/example_test.go` — runnable agent flows.
- `go doc github.com/univeros/polaris.go/<package>` — every exported identifier is documented.
- `internal/apispec/api/**.yaml` — every route: method, path, auth, permissions, input, output, errors.
- `API.md` — what is stable in v0.x (the host surface, the plugin SDK) and what may change.
- `docs/decisions.md` — every design decision, with the reason.
